subject: dsa
title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
summary: An in-order traversal of a BST visits values in sorted order. Walk left, then the node, then right, counting visits; the kth node visited is the kth smallest, and you can stop the moment you reach it.
problem: Return the kth smallest value in a binary search tree. Here k = 3.

steps.caption: In-order traversal of a BST (left, node, right) visits values in sorted order. Count nodes as you visit and stop at the kth. Here k = 3.
Go as far left as possible. 1 is the smallest value — the 1st visited.
1 has a right child 2, which comes next — the 2nd visited.
Back up to the root 3 — the 3rd value visited.
k = 3, so we stop here — the 3rd smallest is 3. We never even visit 4.
